data.about: Three welded steel boxes, each contributing its own weight. Parallel forces have no crossing point at all, so the trial funicular is the only way to place their resultant — and here the position IS the answer: if the resultant falls outside the patch where the sculpture touches the ground, it tips. Drag the boxes and watch the verdict flip.

steps.caption: EX 1 task 3: a sculpture of three welded steel boxes, standing free on the ground — where does its weight act, and does it stand up?
steps.title: The exercise

steps.caption: left: the three boxes; each weight acts as a vertical force through its own centroid (green, dash-dot lines of action)
steps.title: The sculpture and its weights

steps.caption: right: three parallel weights laid tip to tail make one straight load line — the resultant is obviously vertical and equal to their sum. Its POSITION is the whole question
steps.title: The load line

steps.caption: right: a trial pole and its rays to every division of the load line (drag the pole — nothing about the answer depends on it)
steps.title: Pick any pole o

steps.caption: left: start anywhere on the first line of action and draw one string per ray, turning at each line of action
steps.title: The trial funicular

steps.caption: left: the first and last strings, extended (dashed), meet at S — the resultant passes through it
steps.title: Close it: the point S

steps.caption: right: R closes the load line — left: the same vector on the vertical through S, dashed green
steps.title: The resultant — in both diagrams

steps.caption: left: the sculpture only touches the ground under the bottom box (heavy line). The resultant falls OUTSIDE that patch, so the weight cannot be balanced by a contact force — the sculpture tips over the near edge
steps.title: Stable or not?

data.title: EX 1.3 — Resultant of several parallel forces
